scope.purpose: Mechanic-level replication feasibility for the game categories represented in the parent baseline's revenue and popularity lists.
scope.replication_definition: An original implementation of a gameplay pattern, using distinct branding, code, art, audio, text, levels, characters, and economy.

ratings.easy: Local deterministic core with modest original content and no required backend.
ratings.medium: Core is straightforward but needs richer content, performance work, progression, or optional online services.
ratings.hard: Production parity depends on substantial content, an authoritative backend, live operations, security, or platform-controlled capabilities.
ratings.very_hard: Large persistent service with complex economy/social systems and ongoing operations.

cannot_validate_here: WeChat DevTools compile, preview, upload, or simulator behavior
environment_probe.release_gate: Run the official Stable WeChat DevTools on Windows or macOS, then test production-eligible APIs and representative physical devices.

account: Register a Mini Program account with the Game first-level category.
Obtain an AppID; a test account cannot validate commercial features or upload/release.
Complete platform identity, qualification, privacy, content review, and capability eligibility requirements applicable to the game.
toolchain: Use the official Stable WeChat DevTools on Windows or macOS.
Import a native project or an engine export.
Test both DevTools and physical WeChat clients.

runtime.rendering: Full-screen Canvas 2D or WebGL-family host rendering
runtime.adapter_warning: weapp-adapter is user code, is not part of the base library, and does not emulate a complete browser.

production_network: No direct IP address or localhost

hard_blockers.reason: wx.login issues a short-lived code under a WeChat AppID for server-side exchange to openid and session data.
hard_blockers.substitute: Guest account, passkey, Apple/Google/OAuth, and optional account linking.

hard_blockers.capability: Same-game WeChat friend data and ranking
hard_blockers.reason: Friend cloud storage is authorization-gated, restricted to the open-data domain, and the WeChat graph is not exportable.
hard_blockers.substitute: Developer-owned friends/follows, invite codes, and global or cohort leaderboards.

hard_blockers.capability: Midas virtual currency or item payment
hard_blockers.reason: wx.requestMidasPayment requires WeChat/Midas runtime eligibility, offer configuration, and compliant server-side order handling.
hard_blockers.substitute: Web checkout where permitted or Apple/Google in-app purchase with a developer-owned entitlement ledger.

hard_blockers.capability: WeChat share cards, conversation selection, launch query, and group context
hard_blockers.reason: These are WeChat-owned distribution surfaces exposed through wx sharing and launch APIs.
hard_blockers.substitute: Web Share, URLs, QR/referral codes, Universal Links, and App Links.

hard_blockers.capability: WeChat rewarded, interstitial, and banner inventory
hard_blockers.reason: Ad APIs require approved WeChat ad units, runtime inventory, and policy compliance.
hard_blockers.substitute: A web/mobile ad network or a non-ad economy.

hard_blockers.reason: AppID category, qualifications, privacy disclosures, content review, and API permissions are controlled by the platform.
hard_blockers.substitute: Publish on the web or app stores under their independent rules.

hard_blockers.reason: Production requests require registered HTTPS/WSS domains, valid certificates, and an ICP-filed domain.
hard_blockers.substitute: Provision compliant China-facing domains and infrastructure.

engine_options.name: Cocos / Cocos Creator
engine_options.license_note: The engine is open source; verify the exact editor and engine version terms selected for production.

categories.category: Tile match and casual logic puzzle
categories.backend_trust_model: local for core; optional server-validated events and leaderboard
categories.recommended_engine: Phaser for web probe; Cocos for WeChat production
acceptance_checks: Deterministic board model has replayable tests.
Every generated or authored level passes solvability policy.
Touch selection and occlusion work on small screens.
Offline play survives pause, kill, and cold restart.

categories.backend_trust_model: local for core; optional cloud save, events, and leaderboard
acceptance_checks: Scene authoring exports stable hit regions and z-order.
Asset bundles meet cold-start and cache budgets.
Hints never expose an invalid or already-found target.
Zoom, pan, and touch targets pass small-device tests.

categories.backend_trust_model: local; optional cloud events and leaderboard
categories.recommended_engine: Phaser for web probe; Cocos for WeChat production
acceptance_checks: Solver verifies every level and records a solution bound.
Drag collision cannot create overlapping or impossible state.
Undo and save restore exact board state.
Hint logic advances toward a valid solution.
A solver validates all levels.
Direction, collision, and release order are deterministic.
Color and shape cues remain understandable without relying on color alone.
Undo and restart are lossless.

categories.backend_trust_model: local; server validation for competitive score
acceptance_checks: Grid transitions and scoring are deterministic.
Replay input can reproduce a submitted score.
Touch controls remain responsive at frame drops.
Presentation and rule variations receive legal review.
Fixed-step simulation gives consistent landings across frame rates.
Press duration and interruption behavior are tested.
Pause/background cannot advance or corrupt a run.
Competitive submissions include replay or server-verifiable evidence.

categories.backend_trust_model: local campaign; server-owned events, economy, and competitive results
acceptance_checks: Dictionary and answer data have editorial and licensing provenance.
Combat simulation is deterministic and data-driven.
Balance tools can simulate waves and upgrades.
Purchases and event rewards are server-authoritative.

categories.backend_trust_model: local deterministic combat; authoritative progression, economy, events, and purchases
acceptance_checks: Low-tier devices sustain the target frame budget at worst-case entity count.
Seeded combat replays reproduce results.
Object pooling prevents avoidable frame-time and memory spikes.
Progression grants and purchases are idempotent and auditable.

categories.backend_trust_model: local board with server-authoritative timers, events, economy, and purchases for production
acceptance_checks: Every merge transition preserves inventory invariants.
Save schema is versioned and migration-tested.
Authoritative time is used for valuable timers.
Offline and server state reconcile without duplication.

categories.backend_trust_model: local prototype; authoritative cloud economy and events for production
acceptance_checks: State snapshot and event-log recovery are tested.
Remote assets follow versioned cache and eviction policy.
Device clock changes cannot create valuable resources.
Cloud conflict policy is explicit and observable.

categories.backend_trust_model: authoritative account, inventory, progression, event, and payment services
acceptance_checks: All valuable grants are server-authoritative and idempotent.
Offline rewards use authoritative elapsed time and caps.
Economy simulations cover sources, sinks, and event overlap.
Inventory and purchase changes have immutable audit records.

categories.backend_trust_model: local core; server validation for economy and competitive results
acceptance_checks: Controls are tested across touch sampling rates and aspect ratios.
Worst-case effects meet low-tier frame and memory budgets.
Pause/resume restores simulation and audio safely.
Competitive results have replay or server-side validation.

categories.backend_trust_model: authoritative account, character, inventory, combat result, guild, event, and payment services
acceptance_checks: Content schemas and migration tools support versioned live data.
Combat inputs and rewards are validated by the server.
Asset bundles meet startup, download, cache, and memory budgets.
Operations include rollback, audit, moderation, and incident controls.

categories.backend_trust_model: fully authoritative persistent world, economy, alliance, combat, event, chat, moderation, and payment services
categories.recommended_engine: Cocos client plus purpose-built authoritative backend
acceptance_checks: Server is authoritative for time, movement, combat, inventory, and currency.
Load tests cover peak world and alliance events.
Commands are idempotent and resilient to retries and reconnects.
Shard migration, rollback, disaster recovery, moderation, and audit are rehearsed.

global_acceptance_checklist: Core simulation runs without importing wx, DOM, payment, social, or ad APIs.
Platform services are injected behind typed interfaces.
All names, art, audio, text, levels, characters, and economy are original or properly licensed.
Main package, total code package, remote asset, local cache, memory, and cold-start budgets are measured.
Lifecycle tests cover hide, show, memory warning, process destruction, and cold recovery.
Network tests cover weak connection, timeout, retry, duplicate delivery, reconnect, and version skew.
Optional wx APIs use capability detection and a safe fallback.
Production login, ads, payment, share, privacy, and open-data behavior is tested with an eligible AppID.
Real-device tests cover representative low, middle, and high tiers.
Competitive scores and valuable economy mutations have an explicit trust and anti-cheat model.

wechat_required.architecture: Renderer-independent deterministic core plus typed platform adapters
wechat_required.content: Versioned remote asset bundles on a China-appropriate CDN with a minimal main package
wechat_required.casual_backend: HTTPS API, PostgreSQL, object storage/CDN, with Redis only when ranking or rate limits justify it
wechat_required.rpg_slg_backend: Authoritative services, PostgreSQL, Redis, queue/event pipeline, WebSocket gateway where required, immutable economy audit, observability, and anti-cheat
quality_gates: Official Stable DevTools export on Windows or macOS

web_feasibility_only.architecture: Keep rules and level data independent from Phaser
web_feasibility_only.platform_services: Mock identity, payment, social, ads, and share until gameplay is validated

recommended_stack.first_target: An original tile, parking, or timing puzzle
